listing.description: It takes a single approved key visual and instantly builds out a cohesive 9-frame editorial campaign treatment

modelParameters.prompt:
Analyze this fashion/editorial image and describe its visual DNA. 
Do not describe any people, their appearance, postures, clothing, or accessories. Omit any visible typography or symbols.

Return your response in this exact format:
**Editorial Style:** [Describe the overall editorial genre, mood, and campaign aesthetic — e.g. fashion campaign, editorial, lookbook, avant-garde, commercial, etc.]

**Camera & Lens:** [Angle, focal length, depth of field, framing approach]

**Lighting:** [Light source, quality, direction, hardness/softness, shadows]

**Color Palette:** [Dominant colors, contrast relationships, saturation, tonal mood]

**Backdrop & Scene Setup:** [Exact backdrop, location, surface, background elements, props and set dressing excluding worn items]

**Post-Production Style:** [Retouching style, color grading, sharpness, skin/texture treatment, any compositing or CGI cues]


**Overall Mood & References:** [The feeling, era, or visual references this image evokes]

Act as a Creative Director, Art Director, Editorial Photographer, and Luxury Campaign Storyteller. Analyse the attached reference image to identify: the subject (person), the world/location, lighting logic, mood, color grammar, and any objects already visible in the frame. Then write exactly 9 distinct image-generation prompts for a cohesive high-end editorial storyboard that tells this person's story across 9 completely distinct frames, shot on the same campaign set.


The storyboard must preserve the exact visual world, location, subject identity, lighting, mood, and colour language of the reference image. The reference image defines world, location, subject, atmosphere, and visual style — but NOT pose, framing, camera angle, action, or composition. Every frame must read as a new photograph from the same shoot, with a distinct photographic approach and focal length per frame.


SUPPORTING PROP LOGIC (no product node exists — this is the default, not a fallback):
Study the reference image's setting, mood, and implied lifestyle to infer 2–4 plausible props that would naturally belong to this person in this world (e.g. a water bottle, a cigarette, a bicycle, sunglasses, a tote bag, a paperback, a coffee cup — chosen from what the scene logically suggests, not copied verbatim from this list). Assign these across 2–4 of the 9 frames only. Never place more than one prop per frame unless they form one coherent action (e.g. sunglasses pushed up while gripping bicycle handlebars). Props must feel incidental and lived-in — small narrative texture, never competing with the person as visual hero. In each prop frame, state explicitly how it's held, worn, or positioned. The remaining 5–7 frames carry no added props — pure subject and environment.


Every prompt MUST end with this exact sentence: "Inherit the visual DNA of the attached reference image as a continuous editorial campaign. The environment, architectural backdrop, location setting, lighting style, color grading, mood, texture language, subject/character identity, wardrobe logic, and objects presence must remain EXACTLY consistent with the reference image."


CHARACTER COVERAGE — across the 9 frames you must include:
- At least 2 frames shot from behind (walking away, looking over shoulder, back/shoulders/posture as subject)
- At least 1 frame shot from above (overhead/bird's-eye)
- At least 2 close-up frames (face, hands, expression or feature detail)
- At least 1 wide environmental frame establishing them in the world
- No two frames share the same pose, angle, or body orientation (standing, seated, mid-motion, leaning, turning, reclining, etc.)
- Distinct emotional/narrative beats per frame (arrival, stillness, motion, contemplation, interaction with environment or prop, departure, etc.)


LENS COVERAGE — use a different focal length/approach in every frame. Across the 9 prompts, include: 14mm ultra-wide, 20mm wide architectural, 24mm low-angle hero, 35mm documentary, 50mm natural eye-level, 85mm portrait, 105mm compressed detail, 135mm telephoto, and macro detail. Never repeat camera distance, lens behaviour, or composition type between any two frames.


PHOTOGRAPHIC QUALITY — render every frame to studio-grade fidelity: crisp focus, refined dynamic range, color grading matched to the reference image, and high-fidelity material textures (skin, fabric, surfaces, metal). Skin must show natural, uniform, true-to-life texture (pores, fine detail) — no plastic smoothing, no patchy transitions, no visible repair seams. Lighting must read as professional studio or location lighting with falloff and shadow depth consistent with the reference image's light source.


NO TEXT RULE — strictly forbid any visible text, typography, signage, captions, labels, logos, symbols, brand marks, watermarks, posters, screens, or written elements anywhere in frame — including on any inferred prop (e.g. a water bottle must be unmarked and label-free). Describe any naturally-branded object as unmarked, clean, and label-free while preserving its form and material identity.


FORMAT — each prompt must be 80–150 words, one continuous paragraph, enclosed in quotation marks, separated by exactly ONE blank line. Write like an elite luxury campaign treatment. No bullets, titles, headings, intros, analysis, explanations, closing notes, or numbering outside the quotes. Output ONLY the 9 quoted, numbered paragraphs. Each prompt must include @[595f9105-9c07-4dcd-b52e-51a00b8743bf] description.

9. "A macro detail closing frame, bird’s-eye over the subject’s face and hand as they recline on the glowing floor, one eye half visible beneath the orange fringe while the fingertips hover near the temple, showcasing skin glitter, pore structure, pale brow texture, tiny facial shadows, the polished black nail surface, and a glint from a silver ring. The camera should feel clinical yet poetic, translating the same cool, cinematic blue world into an abstract top-down study with the luxury precision of a campaign beauty insert and the graphic boldness of an art-directed sportswear editorial. Hard lateral light remains consistent, creating sharp micro-contrast without losing depth in the navy shadows. No added props, no text, no branding, only pure subject and atmosphere. Inherit the visual DNA of the attached reference image as a continuous editorial campaign. The environment, architectural backdrop, location setting, lighting style, color grading, mood, texture language, subject/character identity, wardrobe logic, and objects presence must remain EXACTLY consistent with the reference image."

595f9105-9c07-4dcd-b52e-51a00b8743bf.text:
**Editorial Style:** High-concept streetwear editorial with a strong sports-culture underpinning. The aesthetic sits between a youth fashion campaign and an art-directed lookbook — bold, kinetic, and deliberately disorienting. It carries the energy of a mid-2000s European sportswear campaign reinterpreted through a contemporary lens.

**Camera & Lens:** Extreme overhead bird's-eye angle, shot with a wide-to-standard lens (approximately 24–35mm equivalent) creating mild wide-angle distortion that exaggerates perspective. The framing is dynamic and tilted, with the subject placed asymmetrically within the frame to amplify tension and movement.

**Lighting:** Hard, directional natural or artificial sunlight striking from a low lateral angle, casting sharp, defined shadows across the court surface. The contrast is punchy and unforgiving — deep shadows pool in the upper-left corner while the court surface catches strong highlights. No visible fill, giving the image a raw, documentary-adjacent quality.

**Color Palette:** Dominated by a cool cerulean blue from the court surface, contrasted against crisp white lane markings. Deep navy anchors the mid-tones, while a warm coral-salmon accent punctuates the top of the frame. The overall palette is cool-dominant with a single warm counterpoint — high contrast, high saturation, cinematic in tone.

**Backdrop & Scene Setup:** An outdoor athletic running track or sports court with a painted blue rubberized surface and bold white geometric lane markings. The lines curve and intersect dynamically beneath the subject, functioning almost as graphic design elements. The upper-left bleeds into deep shadow suggesting nightfall or heavy shade from surrounding structures.

**Post-Production Style:** Minimal but precise retouching — skin texture is preserved with slight luminosity enhancement. Color grading leans into the cool blue tones of the court while preserving warmth in highlights. Contrast is boosted in post, deepening shadows without crushing them entirely. Sharpness is high across the mid-ground; no heavy compositing detected.

**Overall Mood & References:** The image evokes late-90s to early-2000s European sportswear campaigns — think Adidas archive shoots or early Palace Skateboards lookbooks — filtered through a contemporary editorial sensibility. There's an undercurrent of urban athleticism, youthful defiance, and graphic boldness. The overhead angle and court geometry reference both sports photography and abstract visual art simultaneously.
